newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close higher, focus on red chips.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close higher, focus on red chips.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday, but came off the morning's peaks due to caution regarding the longer term outlook for U.S. and Hong Kong interest rates, brokers said.

"The index stopped short of 12,800 because investors are not too keen on getting in at that level," said Eddie Chan, head of trading at New China Hong Kong. "In the short-term, they're still worried about interest rates."
The Hang Seng Index closed 126.19 points higher at 12,707.04, after shooting to a day's high of 12,758.28 at the start of trading.
Local investors were active, seeking out red chips and second and third line related issues.
Among the favourite red chips, China Resources leaped HK$1.15 to HK$21.20 on heavy trade of HK$235.14 million. The share hit a new intra-day high of HK$21.25.
Cosmos Machinery surged HK$1.245, or 64.51 percent, to HK$3.175 on heavy trade of HK$164.72 million. China Resources's parent is taking a 24.3 percent stake in Cosmos.
Shanghai Industrial put on HK$0.80 to HK$41.00.
